items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: my mother insisted that I go to this other fella I mentioned, who was named Tony Bruno... he ushered me into the living room, during those days, and taught me to play the trumpet.

ctx.x: It seems to me I’ve heard about some other fine musicians who came out of that high school.

Oh sure. About I would say, roughly about ten. For a small town like that, if I may I’ll name some. The concert pianist Don Shirley; Junior Cook, a famous jazz saxophonist; and Gigi Gryce, one of the founders of bebop; well myself. Then we’ve had a fine bunch of musicians, white musicians, one was Tony Bruno, a famous trumpet player, he came out of Pensacola; and then we had Ray Brown was born there, Ray Brown, the famous bass player. So I would say about ten. And one of the, I’ll never be able to reason why…
